original_question: Does every closed simply-connected 4-manifold admit a trisection in which one of the three 4-dimensional pieces is a 4-disk? Equivalently, is every closed simply-connected 4-manifold representable by a trisection having a 4-dimensional sector diffeomorphic to the 4-disk, rather than merely by a trisection in which all three sectors are higher-genus 4-dimensional handlebodies?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1, read together with Proposition 1.2: whether every closed simply-connected PL 4-manifold admits a trisection with one 4-dimensional sector equal to the 4-ball D^4; Proposition 1.2 supplies the paper’s official equivalent reformulation in terms of handle decompositions.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the main mathematical content of the paper’s introduction-level open problem: the ambient class is closed simply-connected 4-manifolds, the object is a trisection, and the distinguished feature is that one 4-dimensional piece should be a 4-disk/4-ball rather than a positive-genus 4-dimensional 1-handlebody.
missing_details: The paper works in the PL category, so the manifold should be stated as a closed connected simply-connected PL 4-manifold.

The trisection should be specified in the standard closed 4-manifold sense: M=H0∪H1∪H2 with each Hi a 4-dimensional 1-handlebody, each Hij=Hi∩Hj a 3-dimensional handlebody, and H0∩H1∩H2 a closed connected surface.
The condition on the preferred sector should be stated precisely as 'one Hi is PL-homeomorphic to D^4', equivalently one trisection parameter ki equals 0.

Your second sentence is not the paper’s official equivalent reformulation. The paper’s proved equivalence is instead with the existence of a handle decomposition lacking in 3-handles, equivalently lacking in 1-handles.
The paper presents this as a narrow introduction-level conjecture tied to the handle-decomposition viewpoint, not as a broader question about arbitrary unbalanced trisections in general.
Connectedness is implicit in the paper’s standing assumptions and should be made explicit in a stand-alone formulation.

Nearby context from Theorem 1.3 matters: it gives the positive family immediately following the conjecture/proposition pair, so the refined question should stay exactly at the conjectural level and not drift to broader trisection-existence questions.
refined_question: Does every closed connected simply-connected PL 4-manifold M admit a trisection M=H0∪H1∪H2 in the sense that each Hi is a 4-dimensional 1-handlebody, each pairwise intersection Hij=Hi∩Hj is a 3-dimensional handlebody, the triple intersection H0∩H1∩H2 is a closed connected surface, and one of the sectors Hi is PL-homeomorphic to the 4-ball D^4 (equivalently, one trisection parameter ki is 0)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently (Proposition 1.2), does every closed connected simply-connected PL 4-manifold admit a handle decomposition lacking in 3-handles, equivalently a handle decomposition lacking in 1-handles?
justification: The draft is aiming at the introduction-level conjecture, not at the later algorithmic or graph-theoretic open problems. The clue is the distinguished D^4-sector condition, which is exactly the trisection-side formulation singled out near Conjecture 1.1 and then sharpened by Proposition 1.2 into a handle-decomposition statement. The nearby published formulation of the same equivalence makes this explicit: a trisection of the relevant kind is one where a 4-dimensional piece is a 4-ball, and the corresponding closed orientable 4-manifolds are characterized by handle decompositions lacking in 3-handles (equivalently, 1-handles). So your draft has the right core idea, but it needs the PL category, the precise trisection data, and the paper’s actual equivalent reformulation.
